To determine the agency bean demand numbers, we downloaded procurement data from the [NYC Good Food Purchasing Dashboard](https://www.nyc.gov/site/foodpolicy/good-food-purchasing/citywidedata.page).

We used the Citywide Data for FY2024–2025, which was the most recent year of data available at the time of this analysis.

The file containing the cleaned and categorized data is: [Public-Dashboard-Data-for-Beans_V4](https://github.com/FoodSystemsModeling/CityFoodPolicy/tree/main/drybeans/data_final/Public-Dashboard-Data-for-Beans_v4.xlsx). 

### Identifying Bean Products

The first step was to filter the data to the WRI category "Beans and pulses (dried)."

EM then manually reviewed the products and sorted them into the following categories:

- Canned
- Bagged
- Frozen
- Pouch
- Bean Product
- Green Beans
- Exclude_Other

The Product Item description was used first to determine the appropriate category. When the product form was included in the description, the item was categorized based on that information.

For example: 

BELLAVISTA; BEANS, BLACK; #10 CAN, 6 PER CASE

was categorized as Canned because the product description indicates that it is a canned product.

For items where the product form was not clear from the description, EM looked up the individual product using the available vendor, brand, and product information to determine the most appropriate category.

All of these classifications are retained in [Public-Dashboard-Data-for-Beans_V4](https://github.com/FoodSystemsModeling/CityFoodPolicy/tree/main/drybeans/data_final/Public-Dashboard-Data-for-Beans_v4.xlsx) so they can be reviewed or updated if needed.

#### Bean Products

Products that contained beans as part of a mixed or prepared product were categorized separately as **Bean Product**.

For these products, EM also added a grouping variable to identify the general type of product. For example, quinoa and black bean veggie patties were grouped as **Burger**, while bean- and lentil-based pastas were grouped as **Pasta/Noodle**.

We kept these products separate because their total weight includes ingredients other than beans. For example, the total weight of a black bean veggie burger includes both the beans and the other ingredients in the burger.

#### Excluded Products

- Green Beans were excluded from the final model data.
- The Exclude_Other category was used for products that appeared under the WRI bean/pulse category but were not relevant bean products for this analysis. This included items such as liquid egg substitutes and meatless chicken substitutes.

### Calculating Agency Demand

For each product category, EM summed the total reported weight in pounds for each agency. For example, the canned bean totals were:

| Agency | Total Weight (lbs) | Total Weight (kg) |
|--------|-------------------:|------------------:|
| ACS    | 50,118             | 22,733.12         |
| DOA    | 3,605              | 1,635.20          |
| DOC    | 430,088            | 195,084.48        |
| DHS    | 79,004             | 35,835.58         |
| H+H    | 134,749            | 61,121.07         |
| HRS    | 2,216,559          | 1,005,413.43      |
| DOE    | 4,625,947          | 2,098,292.55      |

: Canned bean totals by agency {#tbl-canned}

The final model categories are:

- canned
- bagged
- bean_product

Products originally categorized as frozen or pouch were included with the bagged category for the model.

### Weight Used for Agency Demand

For the AMB model, we decided to use the total reported product weight as the agency demand measure rather than converting all products to an estimated edible bean weight.

Based on guidance from MOFP, for canned beans the total weight provided by the supplier likely includes the beans and brine and may also include the can/packaging. Similarly, for bagged dry beans, the total weight generally includes the dry beans and packaging. For frozen and pouch products, we also used the total reported product weight.

For bean_product, the total weight includes the full product and therefore may include ingredients other than beans. These products are kept as their own model category for this reason.

The original file includes conversions to estimated edible bean weight. However, we decided to use total product weight for the model so that the demand measure is consistent with the product weight used in the cost data.

These values should therefore be interpreted as the total reported procurement weight of each product category, rather than the weight of edible beans alone.

### Converting Pounds to Kilograms

EM converted the total weight from pounds to kilograms using:

| Pounds | Kilograms |
|-------:|----------:|
| 1      | 0.453592  |

: Pound-to-kilogram conversion {#tbl-conversion}

### Final Model File

The final model data are in: [agency_beans_v5](https://github.com/FoodSystemsModeling/CityFoodPolicy/tree/main/drybeans/data_final/agency_beans_v5.csv).

Each agency has a separate row for each of the three model product categories. For example, the Department of Education data are:

| Agency            | Abbreviation | Latitude | Longitude | Value | Conversion | Product Type | Demand (kg)    |
|-------------------|--------------|---------:|----------:|------:|------------|--------------|---------------:|
| Dept of Education | DOE          | 40.7255  | -73.7177  | 1     | dry_conv   | canned       | 2,098,292.552  |
| Dept of Education | DOE          | 40.7255  | -73.7177  | 1     | dry_conv   | bagged       | 101,860.8875   |
| Dept of Education | DOE          | 40.7255  | -73.7177  | 1     | dry_conv   | bean_product | 1,000,772.277  |

: Example model data for the Department of Education {#tbl-doe}

The final crosswalk from the manual categories to the model categories is:

| Original Category | Final Model Category |
|-------------------|----------------------|
| Canned            | canned               |
| Bagged/Dried      | bagged               |
| Frozen            | bagged               |
| Pouch             | bagged               |
| Bean Product      | bean_product         |
| Green Beans       | Excluded             |
| Exclude_Other     | Excluded             |

: Crosswalk from manual categories to model categories {#tbl-crosswalk}
